This second compound is proposed to modulate the activity of Lysosomal phospholipase A2, which is ultimately involved in the transport of substrates across cellular membranes, as indicated by its interaction with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The evidence suggests a pathway where p-Coumaryl alcohol, (Z)- may influence the activity of Lysosomal phospholipase A2, which then affects the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The integration of these interactions implies that p-Coumaryl alcohol, (Z)- could exert a modulatory effect on the transport function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3, potentially through the indirect action of the intermediate compound. The strength of the evidence is supported by the final score, but further validation would be required to confirm the direct relationship between p-Coumaryl alcohol, (Z)- and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3.
